title: The Gift That Might Be Wrong

collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — FEARS AND DOUBTS (FEA-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Fears big and small, sensible and not, self-doubt, feeling like a fraud, dread with no reason, wanting and fearing the same thing, and courage that is still frightened. Nobody has to be brave, nobody is mocked, and a fear does not have to be conquered by the end.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks two adults)

collection.description: A villager has carved a gift for a friend and is suddenly sure it is terrible: give it anyway, or keep it for now.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has made (friend) a gift: a little carved bird. (subject.He/she) worked on it for days. Now it's finished and wrapped in a leaf, and (subject) is suddenly sure it's terrible. The beak is too long. One wing is lumpy. (friend) won't like it. (subject) is standing outside (friend)'s hut, unable to knock.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) knocks and hands it over without a word. (friend) unwraps it and goes very quiet. Then (friend.he/she) says, "I love it. Is that a heron?" It is not a heron. "Yes," says (subject). (friend) puts it on the shelf by (friend.his/her) sleeping mat, where it stays for years, as a heron.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) walks home with the bird still in (subject.his/her) hand. (subject.He/she) puts it on (subject.his/her) own shelf. Every time (subject.he/she) looks at it, it looks a little less terrible. A month later, (subject.he/she) gives it to (friend) after all. (friend) loves it. (subject) wonders why (subject.he/she) waited, and then remembers exactly why.
